sections.skill: Compare running a model through a provider with running one locally

questions.prompt: What happens when you use a model through a provider?

choices.text: The model always runs entirely on your own phone without using the internet at all
Your request goes to the provider's computers

questions.correct_answer: Your request goes to the provider's computers
questions.intro: A model can run in two places. Through a PROVIDER (in the cloud): your request goes over the internet to the provider's computers. Benefits: powerful models, no special hardware, and the provider handles updates. Costs and concerns: fees, dependence on the internet and the provider, and your data leaving your device. ON YOUR OWN DEVICE (locally): you download a model and run it yourself. Benefits: data can stay on your device and it can work offline. Costs: capable hardware, usually smaller or less capable models, and you handle setup and updates.

questions.prompt: What is a benefit of running a model locally?

choices.text: You always get the most powerful models available, which are larger than any cloud model

sections.skill: Compare cloud and local models with eating out and cooking at home

questions.prompt: A restaurant is like what?

choices.text: Running a model locally on your own laptop, using your own electricity and equipment

questions.intro: EATING AT A RESTAURANT is like using a provider: skilled chefs and big kitchens, no equipment needed at home, but you pay each time, travel there, and others handle your food. COOKING AT HOME is like running a model locally: you need a kitchen and skills, meals may be simpler, and you clean up, but you control the ingredients and nobody else sees your plate. Neither is always better; it depends on the meal.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Avoid assumptions about local and cloud

questions.prompt: Is a local app automatically private?

choices.text: Yes, because every app that runs on your own device keeps all data on the device forever
No; some still send data online

questions.correct_answer: No; some still send data online
questions.intro: Local is not automatically private or free. Some local apps still send data online, so check their settings. Running large models can need expensive hardware and use a lot of electricity, and keeping models and software updated, including security fixes, is your job. Cloud is not automatically unsafe: providers may offer strong security and data controls. Choose based on the task: sensitivity of the data, needed capability, budget, and who will maintain it.

questions.prompt: Is running a large model locally automatically free?
